newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - European OTC debt vol slightly better bid.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - European OTC debt vol slightly better bid.

text.p: European OTC debt volatility recovered slightly on Friday after alarmingly high U.S. payroll numbers pushed debt markets lower, but dealers said the options market had been weak going into the data.
Contracts at the short end attracted some interest, with bullish Euromark and Pibor strategies going through.
"Volatility (in Europe) has come off during the course of the week," said a dealer at a U.S. house in London.
U.S. nonfarm payroll data rose 262,000 in December, against forecasts for a 192,000 rise. The figures pushed U.S. Treasuries sharply lower and European markets quickly followed suit.

Dealers said the fall in volatilities, notably in February options, earlier in the week was a natural reaction after levels had been inflated over the holiday period. They said locals in London had pushed up volatility in a thin market.
Three-month OTC Bund price volatility at 1605 GMT was around six percent, little changed from the start of the week. Three-month BTP vols were at 9.1 percent, down from 9.4 on Monday.
Luke White, broker at Fimat Futures in London, noted bullish combo trades in Euromarks and call ladders in Pibor ahead of the data.
"Most of the trades today have been in the short end and have been looking at bullish scenarios," White said.
March 97.00/10/30 call ladders attracted sizeable trade, as did June 97.10/20/40 call ladders.
In Euromarks, there was heavy trade in a June 96.75/97.00 combo, where players bought 97.00 calls and sold 96.75 puts. The strategy foresees a low German interest rate environment.
